title: Choose the results layout
question: Three structures for the Bayesian results panel, all in the AinaDara house style. Lock one, steer it, or re-roll.

options.label: The course timeline
options.lineage: medication administration record, read left to right
options.thesis: Results open on the patient's course (doses, levels, SCr) with the verdict standing at the 'now' end of it.
options.viewport: A full-width course strip (dose bars as wide as each infusion, level dots, SCr ticks), the verdict — 1 g IV q12h · AUC 434, likely 330 to 650 · confidence — anchored at its right edge; the fan-chart curve directly beneath on the same time axis; evidence below as hairline sections.
options.risk: The verdict sits beside the timeline rather than above everything, so it must be set large enough to win the first glance.

options.label: Verdict and evidence tabs
options.thesis: One verdict block on top; the evidence lives behind five tabs so only one question is on screen at a time.
options.viewport: Verdict block across the full results width (order string in DM Serif, AUC as a lopsided bar with a 20-dot plot over the target band, confidence word and reason, next step); under it a tab row — Curve · Models · Fit · Regimens · Explore — and one panel.
options.risk: Evidence behind tabs is evidence nobody opens; the verdict must carry every safety flag itself.

regions.label: tabs: curve · models · fit · regimens · explore

options.label: The matrix is the answer
options.thesis: The dose × interval exposure matrix is the result; the recommended cell is the answer and any cell can be selected.
options.viewport: A verdict strip on top naming the selected regimen; below it the matrix at full weight with the recommended cell outlined in terracotta, and beside it the fan-chart curve and trough for whichever cell is selected; models, fit and clearance follow as footnotes.
options.risk: A grid of 32 regimens asks the reader to choose; the recommended cell must read as the answer, not one option among many.
